clue.text: Plays chess and adjusts to new position?

definitions.meaning: to play chess is to take a turn on the board, shifting a piece
to shift oneself to a new spot or take action, figuratively stirring oneself

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both taking a turn in a board game and, generally, stirring to act or relocate.

clue.text: Line on board, one grabbed by piece with cover

indicators.note: the word one is seized and held within the word for piece

parts.note: a chessman is a piece, so MAN
one is the Roman numeral I
a sheet is a cover, as on a bed

explanation.surface: A chess piece with a cloth over it sits on the board alongside a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line on board' sounds like a chessboard rank, but the board is a boat's deck and the line a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainsheet is the rope controlling the mainsail on a sailing boat, so a line aboard.

clue.text: High-flier with set of pieces and heart in chess

parts.note: a kit is a set of parts or equipment

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here of chess

explanation.surface: A star player with a full chess set shows heart in the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is a bird of prey and also a toy flown high on a string.

clue.text: Foils Spassky's opening? Possibly misread

indicators.note: the opening of a name is its initial letter, from Spassky's
possibly signals that the letters of misread may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Boris Spassky's chess opening might have been misread as a pair of blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foils' looks like a verb (thwarts) but is a plural noun: fencing swords.
explanation.definitionFit: Foils are light swords, and swords worn at the belt are weapons carried at one's flank.

clue.text: Pawn I advanced with great enthusiasm

parts.note: a pawn is a chessman, so MAN
A stands for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A chess player pushes a pawn forward with real gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: Mania is a craze or obsessive passion for something.

clue.text: Kasparov's ultimate sharpness produces a blank stare?

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its final one, here of Kasparov's

parts.note: acuity is sharpness of mind or sight

explanation.surface: Garry Kasparov's famous keenness at the board leaves an opponent gaping vacantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacuity is emptiness of mind, the vacant look of a blank expression.

clue.text: Mark's taken in by fool's mate

definitions.text: Mark's taken in by fool's mate

parts.words: Mark's taken in by fool's mate
parts.note: the punctuation sign written in Mark's is also enclosed in the chess phrase fool's mate, between the l and the s

explanation.surface: A chess player called Mark is caught out by the quickest checkmate there is.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a person's name, but it is a punctuation mark: the one inside the word fool's.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised comma marking possession, as in fool's, is a punctuation mark.

clue.text: Phrase indicating prime mover, with Lasker initially involved

indicators.note: the initial is wrapped up inside the word for prime mover

parts.note: the prime mover of anything is its cause

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of Lasker

explanation.surface: An expression pointing to who set things in motion, with chess champion Emanuel Lasker involved from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause is a group of words with its own verb, part of a sentence.

clue.text: Reduced pain of mate, repelled small attacking force

parts.note: a pal is a mate or friend

indicators.note: repelled means pushed back, so the word for the attacking force is turned round

parts.note: a detail is a small detachment of troops given a task

explanation.surface: A soldier eased a friend's suffering after a minor assault was beaten back.
explanation.definitionFit: To palliate is to ease suffering without curing its cause, as in hospice care.

clue.text: Audacity in hints of nasty early combination against king

indicators.note: a hint of a word is its first letter, taken from nasty, early, combination

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A ruthless opening combination aimed at the king shows boldness.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck is informal British slang for cheek or brazen nerve.

clue.text: Indication of rank occupied by queen for game

indicators.note: the word for rank badge is filled by the abbreviation for queen

parts.note: a sash worn across the body shows rank or office

explanation.surface: A queen sitting on a rank of the chessboard is a sign of a certain game plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' suggests a chessboard row, but it means status, shown by a ceremonial sash.
explanation.definitionFit: Squash is a racket sport played in a walled court.

clue.text: Model short exhibition by one grandmaster

indicators.note: short means the word for exhibition loses its final letter

parts.note: a parade is a public display or exhibition
one is the Roman numeral I
GM is the chess abbreviation for grandmaster

explanation.surface: A brief demonstration game by a single grandmaster serves as an example to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a typical example or pattern, a template others copy.

clue.text: One of many floorings in chess scene?

definitions.meaning: a kind of tongue-and-groove timber used for floors and panelling
read whimsically as the board used in a chess contest

explanation.definitionFit: Matchboard is grooved timber planking, and split up it suggests the board where a competitive game is played.

clue.text: Mate? Seek information about "End of game"

indicators.note: about means the word for consult goes around the final letter

parts.note: to refer to a source is to consult it for facts

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, from game

explanation.surface: A partner looks up information about how chess games end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like checkmate, but it is a ship's officer: a reefer is a midshipman.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefer is old naval slang for a midshipman, a junior officer who helped reef sails.

clue.text: Subtle hasty mate, not Capablanca's last gem

indicators.note: subtle in its sense of crafty or cunning signals that the letters are slyly rearranged
the last letter of Capablanca's is taken, and the word not tells us it is dropped from the mix

explanation.surface: A quick, sly checkmate that the Cuban champion Capablanca never played is a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HASTY MATE, minus the A that ends Capablanca, rearrange to the answer; 'not' signals that removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple variety of quartz prized as a gemstone.

clue.text: Plays great moves, then fades

indicators.note: moves signals that the letters of great are shifted into a new order

parts.note: to die away is to fade, so DIES

explanation.surface: A player makes brilliant moves and then runs out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' looks like a verb about a chess player, but it is the plural noun for dramas; 'moves' is the anagram signal, not chess moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragedies are dramas, plays ending in disaster for the hero.

clue.text: Like a pocket chess set, say, affording endless study over board

definitions.text: Like a pocket chess set, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second
endless means the word for study loses its final letter

parts.note: to pore over something is to study it closely
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A pocket chess set lets you study the game anywhere without a full-sized board.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable means easily carried, which a travel-sized set is.

clue.text: Chess situation created by opening

definitions.meaning: the arrangement of pieces on the board at a given moment

explanation.definitionFit: Position means both the layout of pieces at a moment in a game and a job vacancy.

clue.text: Sensational play from singular pawn and queen

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
to hock something is to pawn it
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A lurid move results from a lone pawn and the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pawn' looks like the chess piece but is the verb: hock means pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A shocker is a lurid, sensational story or drama.

clue.text: A bishop's pulled back, reinforcing change in defence

indicators.note: reinforcing means strengthening from within, so the reversed letters go inside

parts.note: change is loose cash

indicators.note: pulled back means these letters are read from right to left

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop retreats to shore up a switch in the defensive setup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled back' turns A and B into BA, which goes inside CASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A casbah is the citadel or fortress of a North African city.

clue.text: Crazy, with queen trapped, and fractious

indicators.note: trapped means the queen letter is caught inside the word for crazy

parts.note: batty is informal for crazy
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A mad player with the queen trapped turns peevish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bratty describes a child behaving like a spoilt, irritable brat.

clue.text: To stretch e.g. Tal, one moved deviously

indicators.note: moving letters in a crafty way signals that e.g., Tal and one are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mikhail Tal, for example, could prolong a game with one sly move.
explanation.walkthrough: Mikhail Tal was a world chess champion famed for tricky attacking play.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to lengthen or extend.

clue.text: E.g. Bobby Fischer, one fired with class

indicators.note: fired means sacked, so the letter for one is thrown out

parts.note: the chess champion Bobby Fischer is an example of a genius
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Bobby Fischer, a fired-up chess champion, was in a class of his own.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus is a biological class or category of related species.

clue.text: Smoothly played game by a leading pair in tournament

parts.note: a leg is one game in a series, as in darts

indicators.note: the leading pair of a word is its first two letters, from tournament

explanation.surface: A game played fluently by someone at the top of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is a musical direction for notes played smoothly and connected.

clue.text: Pluck calls for mastery, sacrificing pawn for

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Pluck calls for mastery, sacrificing pawn for', looks cut short: GRIP (mastery) with P swapped needs a word for T after 'for', and 'calls' has no job
annotationWithheld.clue: Pluck calls for mastery, sacrificing pawn for

clue.text: Rook — second piece short

indicators.note: short means the word for the piece loses its last letter

parts.note: the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A rook is the second chess piece you lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like the chess piece, but it is a verb: to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook or skin someone is to cheat or fleece them.

clue.text: Knight's returned in exchange for one maybe exploiting defence strategy

indicators.note: in puts the turned title inside the word for exchange

parts.note: to barter is to exchange goods

indicators.note: returned means the title for a knight is turned round

parts.note: a knight is styled Sir

explanation.surface: A knight is given back in a trade for a piece useful in a defensive setup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defence strategy' suggests chess, but it is a courtroom defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister argues cases in court, often presenting a client's defence.

clue.text: Brochure from pro puts odd features of chess in new perspective

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: seeing the letters from a fresh angle signals that they are rearranged
the odd features are the odd-numbered letters of chess

explanation.surface: A professional reframes the quirkier aspects of chess in a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of PUTS plus CES, the first, third and fifth letters of chess.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospectus is a printed booklet describing a school, company or offer.
